# B&B Merì

> Bed & Breakfast nel quartiere Castello, centro storico di Cagliari: camere con bagno privato, Wi-Fi gratuito, aria condizionata, acqua potabile dal rubinetto e transfer su richiesta.
> Bed & Breakfast in the Castello district, the historic centre of Cagliari, Sardinia: rooms with private bathroom, free Wi-Fi, air conditioning, drinkable tap water and transfer on request.

Sito ufficiale / Official website: https://www.meribnb.it/ (italiano, English, français, español).
Aggiornato il / Last updated: 2026-11-22.

## In breve (italiano)

- Dove: Via Alberto Lamarmora 18, 09124 Cagliari — quartiere Castello, centro storico

- Check-in: dalle 15:00 alle 20:00, anche online prima dell'arrivo
- Check-out: entro le 10:30
- Colazione: non inclusa
- Servizi: Wi-Fi gratuito, aria condizionata e riscaldamento, acqua potabile dal rubinetto, transfer su richiesta
- Animali: non ammessi

## Domande frequenti (italiano)

- **Come arrivo dall'aeroporto?** In treno da Elmas Aeroporto alla stazione di Cagliari in Piazza Matteotti (circa 10 minuti), poi bus CTM linea 7, che ferma proprio davanti a casa.
- **Castello è ZTL? Dove parcheggio?** Sì, Castello è zona a traffico limitato: non entrate in auto nel quartiere. Il parcheggio gratuito più vicino è in Viale Buoncammino; a pagamento ci sono le aree e il multipiano di Viale Regina Elena, collegati a Castello da ascensori pubblici. Tutti i dettagli, con mappe e tariffe, sono nella nostra guida ai parcheggi: https://www.meribnb.it/parcheggi/
- **A che ora sono il check-in e il check-out?** Il check-in è dalle 15:00 alle 20:00; per orari diversi basta avvisarci. Il check-out è entro le 10:30. Potete fare il check-in online in anticipo dal pulsante in cima alla pagina.
- **La colazione è inclusa?** No, la colazione non è inclusa nel prezzo. Nei dintorni ci sono bar e caffè dove fare colazione, a pochi minuti a piedi.
- **Come si prenota? C'è uno sconto prenotando direttamente?** Sì: prenotando per telefono al 352 036 8357 avete il 10% di sconto rispetto alla tariffa di Booking. Potete scriverci anche su WhatsApp allo stesso numero o via email a meri.bnb.cagliari@gmail.com: rispondiamo in giornata.
- **Le camere hanno il bagno privato?** Sì, ogni camera ha il bagno privato con doccia, asciugacapelli e set di cortesia.
- **Quante persone può ospitare la camera?** La Camera Matrimoniale ospita fino a 2 persone, con un letto matrimoniale. La Camera con Cucina al momento non è disponibile.
- **Ci sono Wi-Fi e aria condizionata?** Sì: il Wi-Fi è gratuito e veloce in tutta la struttura, e ogni camera ha aria condizionata e riscaldamento autonomi.
- **Il transfer è disponibile?** Sì, su richiesta: scriveteci in anticipo per organizzarlo.
- **L'acqua del rubinetto è potabile?** Sì, l'acqua del rubinetto è potabile: fresca e buona da bere.
- **Cosa c'è da vedere vicino al B&B?** Siete nel cuore di Castello: la Cattedrale è a 2 minuti a piedi, il Bastione di Saint Remy a 3 e la Torre dell'Elefante a 4. Trovate l'itinerario completo a piedi, con tempi e mappe, nella nostra guida: https://www.meribnb.it/cosa-vedere-a-castello/
- **Quanto dista la spiaggia?** La spiaggia del Poetto, 8 km di sabbia bianca, dista circa 6 km: 15 minuti in bus o 10 in auto.
- **Sono ammessi animali?** Al momento non possiamo accogliere animali domestici.

## Frequently asked questions (English)

- **How do I get there from the airport?** By train from Elmas Aeroporto to Cagliari station in Piazza Matteotti (about 10 minutes), then CTM bus line 7, which stops right outside our door.
- **Is Castello a ZTL? Where can I park?** Yes, Castello is a limited-traffic zone: please don't drive into the quarter. The nearest free parking is on Viale Buoncammino; paid options are the street areas and the multi-storey car park on Viale Regina Elena, linked to Castello by public lifts. All the details, with maps and prices, are in our parking guide: https://www.meribnb.it/en/parking/
- **What are the check-in and check-out times?** Check-in is from 3:00 PM to 8:00 PM; just let us know if you need a different time. Check-out is by 10:30 AM. You can complete online check-in in advance using the button at the top of the page.
- **Is breakfast included?** No, breakfast is not included in the price. There are bars and cafés for breakfast a few minutes' walk away.
- **How do I book? Is there a discount for booking direct?** Yes: book by phone on +39 352 036 8357 and you get 10% off the Booking.com rate. You can also message us on WhatsApp at the same number or email us at meri.bnb.cagliari@gmail.com: we reply within the day.
- **Do the rooms have a private bathroom?** Yes, every room has a private bathroom with shower, hairdryer and toiletries.
- **How many guests can the room sleep?** The Double Room sleeps up to 2 guests in a double bed. The Room with Kitchenette is currently unavailable.
- **Is there Wi-Fi and air conditioning?** Yes: free, fast Wi-Fi throughout the property, and every room has its own air conditioning and heating.
- **Is a transfer available?** Yes, on request: write to us in advance to arrange it.
- **Is the tap water drinkable?** Yes, the tap water is drinkable: fresh and good to drink.
- **What is there to see near the B&B?** You're in the heart of Castello: the Cathedral is a 2-minute walk away, the Bastione di Saint Remy 3 minutes and the Elephant Tower 4. Our guide has the full walking tour, with times and maps: https://www.meribnb.it/en/things-to-see-in-castello/
- **How far is the beach?** Poetto beach, 8 km of white sand, is about 6 km away: 15 minutes by bus or 10 by car.
- **Are pets allowed?** Unfortunately we cannot accommodate pets at the moment.

## Getting here (English)

- **From the airport by train**: From Elmas Aeroporto station, a short walk from the terminal, the train takes you in about 10 minutes to Cagliari station in Piazza Matteotti (ticket about €1.30, a train roughly every 20 minutes).
- **Then bus no. 7**: In front of the station, take CTM bus line 7: it climbs up to Castello and stops right outside our door.
- **Coming by car? Here's where to park**: Castello is a ZTL: leave the car outside the quarter. The nearest free parking is on Viale Buoncammino; paid options are the street areas and the multi-storey car park on Viale Regina Elena, linked to Castello by public lifts. Read our full parking guide, with maps and prices →
- **Transfer on request**: Rather be picked up? We can arrange a transfer to and from the property: just ask us in advance.

## Location: walking times from the B&B (English)

- Cathedral of Santa Maria: 2 min walk
- Elephant Tower: 4 min walk
- Via Roma and the port: 10 min walk
- Poetto beach: 15 min by bus or car
- Cagliari-Elmas Airport: 15 min by car

## Parking near Castello (checked October 2026; prices may change)

- **Viale Buoncammino** (Free): Cost: free on white lines; Walk to the B&B: about 10 minutes, mostly flat; Way into Castello: Porta Cristina → Piazza Arsenale. The panoramic avenue along the ridge, with views over the whole city: it's the nearest free parking. Look for a space as close as possible to Porta Cristina, then walk into Castello through Piazza Arsenale. Watch out: on part of the avenue the lines are blue, which means paid. In high season it can be full.
- **Blue lines, free at certain times** (Free evenings and Sundays): Free: Sundays and public holidays; Monday–Saturday 1–4 PM and 8 PM–9 AM; Paid: Monday–Saturday 9 AM–1 PM and 4–8 PM. Blue-line spaces are only paid at certain times. If you arrive in the evening or at the weekend you can also leave the car on the blue lines near Castello (Viale Buoncammino, Viale Regina Elena) for free — just remember to pay when the paid hours start. Always check the sign for that area.
- **Regina Elena Alta area (APCOA)** (Cheapest): Cost: €0.50 the first hour, then €1 per hour — €2.50 per day maximum; Paid hours: Monday–Saturday 9 AM–1 PM and 4–8 PM; Walk to the B&B: about 10 minutes using the lifts. Open-air blue-line spaces on the upper part of Viale Regina Elena, below the walls of Castello. With its €2.50 daily cap, it's the best-value paid option if you stay several days. From here, go up to Castello with the public lifts.
- **Regina Elena Bassa 1 and 2 areas (APCOA)** (Paid): Cost: Bassa 1: €1 per hour, €8 per day maximum · Bassa 2: €0.50 the first hour, then €1, €7.50 maximum; Paid hours: Monday–Saturday 9 AM–1 PM and 4–8 PM; Walk to the B&B: about 10–15 minutes using the lifts. More blue-line spaces on the lower part of Viale Regina Elena: handy when Regina Elena Alta is full.
- **Regina Elena multi-storey car park (APCOA)** (Covered · 24/7): Cost: about €1.70 per hour, €10 per day maximum; Hours: open 24/7; Address: Viale Regina Elena 17; Walk to the B&B: about 10 minutes using the lifts. A covered car park at the foot of the walls: the easiest, most worry-free choice if you leave the car for your whole stay. Once outside, the public lifts on Viale Regina Elena take you up to Castello.
- **Blue lines in the centre** (Paid): Cost: about €1 per hour (in some areas €0.50 the first hour), €10 per day maximum; Paid hours: Monday–Saturday 9 AM–1 PM and 4–8 PM; free on Sundays and public holidays; How to pay: at the parking meter or with an app (for example Telepass or MoneyGo). You'll also find them on part of Viale Buoncammino and in the streets around Castello. Prices vary from area to area: always read the sign.
- **Former Unione Sarda lifts → Piazza Palazzo** (Closest to the B&B): From: Viale Regina Elena, by the Terrapieno; To: Piazza Palazzo, next to the Cathedral: a few steps from the B&B; Cost: free. Two lifts in a row: the first goes up from Viale Regina Elena to the Terrapieno, the second, a panoramic one, arrives in Piazza Palazzo. It's the most direct link to the B&B. In summer they may stop during the hottest hours.
- **Saint Remy lift → Bastion** (Free): From: Viale Regina Elena, in the gardens below the walls, about 100 m from Piazza Costituzione; To: Bastione di Saint Remy, then a few minutes on foot; Cost: free. It takes you up to the great terrace of the Bastione di Saint Remy, a few minutes' walk from the B&B. In summer it may also stop during the hottest hours.

## Things to see on foot from the B&B (English)

- **Cathedral of Santa Maria** (2 min walk): Cagliari's cathedral, on Piazza Palazzo, dates back to the Pisans in the 13th century; its Pisan Romanesque façade was rebuilt in the 20th century. Inside, don't miss the two pulpits by Master Guglielmo, made from a single pulpit carved in the 12th century for Pisa Cathedral, and the Crypt of the Martyrs, cut into the rock.
- **Palazzo Regio and Palazzo di Città** (2 min walk): On the same square stand the Palazzo Regio, the former viceroys' residence that hosted the Savoy court in the early 19th century, and the Palazzo di Città, the old town hall, now used for exhibitions by the city museums.
- **San Pancrazio Tower** (5 min walk): Built by the Pisans in 1305 on the highest part of Castello, it is the twin of the Elephant Tower. When it's open you can climb to the top for views over the city, the gulf and the lagoons.
- **Cittadella dei Musei** (7 min walk): On Piazza Arsenale, in the old arsenal, you'll find the National Archaeological Museum, with Nuragic bronze figurines and some of the Giants of Mont'e Prama, and the National Art Gallery. It's the place to discover the history of Sardinia.
- **Porta Cristina and Viale Buoncammino** (10 min walk): From Piazza Arsenale you leave the walls through Porta Cristina, a 19th-century neoclassical gate, and reach Viale Buoncammino: a tree-lined avenue along the ridge with views over the city and the lagoons.
- **Bastione di Santa Croce and the old Ghetto** (5 min walk): On the west side of the walls, the Bastione di Santa Croce is a panoramic terrace much loved at sunset. Next to it are the former Jewish Ghetto, now an exhibition space, and the Basilica of Santa Croce, built where the synagogue once stood.
- **Elephant Tower** (4 min walk): Built in 1307 by Giovanni Capula, the architect of the San Pancrazio Tower, it takes its name from the small marble elephant on its façade. It was one of Castello's gates: walk through it to head down to the lower town.
- **Bastione di Saint Remy** (3 min walk): Cagliari's landmark, built between the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with a grand staircase rising from Piazza Costituzione. From the Terrazza Umberto I the view takes in the rooftops of Villanova and Marina, the port and the Gulf of Angels.
- **Marina quarter and Via Roma** (10 min walk): Walking down from Castello you reach Marina, the quarter between the walls and the port, with lanes full of trattorias and small shops. Under the arcades of Via Roma you can stroll while watching the ships in the harbour.
- **Roman Amphitheatre and Botanical Garden** (15 min walk): The amphitheatre, from the 2nd century AD, is largely carved into the rock of the hill. A few steps away is the University Botanical Garden, a green oasis with Mediterranean and tropical plants.
- **Poetto beach and Sella del Diavolo** (15 min by bus or car): Poetto is the city's beach: about 8 km of pale sand with kiosks and beach clubs. At the Marina Piccola end, the Sella del Diavolo headland has panoramic trails with superb views over the gulf.
- **Molentargius park** (15 min by car): Between the city and Poetto, the Molentargius-Saline nature park protects lagoons and old salt pans where pink flamingos live. You can explore it on foot or by bike.
